audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer names Scrap Shield as the matchup-defining ability in the focus, cooldown block, Do's and report ('Shield + speed on demand — trade just after he burns it'). It is a 6-second self-shield with no offensive interaction.
audit.why: What actually decides this lane is Electro Harpoon: 850 range, two stored charges, slows and shreds magic resist, and it is the button that glues Lillia into the 600-range Flamespitter cone. Waiting out a 6-second shield is not a plan; waiting out both harpoon charges is.
audit.corrected: Cooldown block, Do's line and report[5] re-pointed at Electro Harpoon with its range and two-charge behaviour.
sources: brief enemyKit W text and 6s cd
brief enemyKit E text (850 range, 2 harpoons)

audit.whatIsWrong: Five chart rows disagreed with the content whys: Levels 2 and 3 were credited to Rumble though the whys call level 2 'a wash' and level 3 Lillia's, Levels 4-5 read Skill though the whys call them her grind window, Level 6 read Skill though the whys call it 'the answer to your kite', and 2+ items read Rumble though the whys say 'genuinely even late'.
audit.why: Rumble's two spikes are Level 6 (The Equalizer carving her hop-lanes) and his first AP item; Lillia's are levels 3-5, when Swirlseed plus stacking speed keeps her outside a 600-range cone.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Skill / Lillia / Lillia / Rumble / Rumble / Skill with ratings 5, 5, 6, 7, 3, 5, 5 as matched full+content pairs.

audit.why: EVEN at 5.5/10 matches 52.58%. Both champions scale on percent-health magic damage, which is why neither owns the late game.

The packet's suspect name 'Full Blooming Blows' is a false positive — correct Riot name with a leading word. Separately, the derived flags on Scrap Shield list knockup and terrain, which Riot's text does not support ('pulls up a shield... and a quick burst of speed'); I trusted the description and did not write either into the page.

edits.before: Q's outer ring on his last-hits plus the passive speed means he literally cannot touch you at level 1.
edits.after: Even at 1 — you have one ability and no kite chain, so farm at range while he shoves with Flamespitter.

edits.before: W sweetspot threat starts — anyone chasing you eats the big hit while your Dream Dust burns their HP bar.
edits.after: Your Q sweetspot poke is real, but without Swirlseed he shields in and out-DPSes you in the cone.

edits.before: Full kit: Q-kite in circles, E from fog for the slow, and the passive speed makes every trade yours to end.
edits.after: Q sweetspot plus the E slow starts the Dream Dust burn and your speed keeps you off his Flamespitter.

edits.before: The lane is a treadmill he can't get off — Q every step-up, kite the Scrap Shield window, and bank Dream Dust burn.
edits.after: Full Blooming Blows plus the compounding burn grinds down anyone who must walk at you — his 600 cone cannot reach.

edits.before: Lilting Lullaby online — your jungler's ganks are now guaranteed, and any overstep becomes a sleep-execute.
edits.after: His 6 answers your kite — The Equalizer cuts your hop-lanes and a harpoon slow pins you in the fire.

edits.before: Liandry's spike — Dream Dust plus the burn melts juggernauts and tanks alike while you jog circles around them.
edits.after: His first AP item turns the harpoon into overheated Flamespitter burst that edges your Liandry's chunk.

edits.before: You're a teamfight nightmare now: sleep two, kite the rest, and let the burn do the bookkeeping.
edits.after: Genuinely even late — you both scale on percent-HP, so avoid his 1v1 and sleep in teamfights.

edits.before: - Rumble Scrap Shield: matchup-defining — Shield + speed on demand — trade just after he burns it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your passive move speed has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Rumble Electro Harpoon: matchup-defining — an 850-range slow that shreds MR and glues you into Flamespitter. Count both charges if you must. - Your passive move speed has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.

edits.before: Shield + speed on demand — trade just after he burns it. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Two harpoons at 850 range slow you into his cone — trade just after he spends them, never before.

edits.before: Track Rumble’s Scrap Shield: Shield + speed on demand — trade just after he burns it. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Rumble’s Electro Harpoon: an 850-range slow that shreds MR — trade only once both charges are spent.

notes: The content layer here is accurate and specific; the fix was the chart (five rows against its own whys) and the full layer's focus on Scrap Shield, which is a 6s self-shield and not the ability that decides anything. focus.text ('Rumble Scrap Shield', 19 chars) and the loading/winCon/tradeBad copies of that focus string are under or built from the same template and still point at the wrong ability — they need the focus regenerated to Electro Harpoon. Derived-flag misfire noted: Scrap Shield carries knockup/terrain flags that Riot's text does not support.
